descripcion: Phrasal verbs are the part of English that looks optional and is not. There is almost always a one-word alternative, and it almost always sounds more formal than the situation needs. Saying *I tolerated it* instead of *I put up with it* is correct English and the wrong register. At B2 the goal is to stop avoiding them.

filas: *pick up the keys* / *pick the keys up*
*put up with*, *look forward to*, *get on with*
cuadroReferencia.notaPie: If you only remember one rule: **a pronoun always goes in the middle.**

ejemplos.texto: *We set off early and checked in without any trouble.*
*It took me months to get used to it.*
*The car broke down and we had to sort it out ourselves.*
*I couldn't put up with the noise any longer.*
*We ran out of money three days before the end.*

notas: Many have a formal one-word twin: *find out / discover*, *put off / postpone*, *look into / investigate*. Both are correct; the phrasal one is normal in speech.
The same phrasal verb can mean very different things. *Pick up* can mean collect, learn, improve or answer the phone. Context decides.
Three-part verbs are where learners most often drop the middle word. *Put up with*, not *put with*.

es.en: Spanish has no phrasal verbs, so the first word that comes to mind is always the Latin-origin one — which exists in English but sits a register higher. That mismatch is why correct English can still sound stiff.
es.es: El español no tiene phrasal verbs, por lo que la primera palabra que viene a la mente suele ser la de origen latino, que existe en inglés pero se sitúa un registro más alto. Ese desajuste explica por qué un inglés correcto puede seguir sonando rígido.

de.en: German separable verbs work much like phrasal verbs (aufgeben – give up, herausfinden – find out), so German speakers use them readily. Many particles even match in meaning (auf – up, aus – out).
de.de: Deutsche trennbare Verben funktionieren ähnlich wie phrasal verbs («aufgeben» – «give up», «herausfinden» – «find out»), daher verwenden Deutschsprachige sie gern. Viele Partikeln stimmen sogar in der Bedeutung überein («auf» – «up», «aus» – «out»).

it.en: Italian verbi sintagmatici (andare via – go away, tirare su – pick up) are a good model for English phrasal verbs. Italian speakers can use them as a bridge instead of defaulting to the Latinate verb.
it.it: I verbi sintagmatici italiani («andare via» – «go away», «tirare su» – «pick up») sono un buon modello per i phrasal verbs inglesi. Gli italofoni possono usarli come ponte invece di ricorrere automaticamente al verbo latino.

fr.en: French has no phrasal verbs, so the first word that comes to mind is the Latinate one (continuer – continue rather than go on). That verb sits a register higher, which is why correct English can still sound stiff.
fr.fr: Le français n'a pas de phrasal verbs, donc le premier mot qui vient à l'esprit est le mot latin («continuer» – «continue» plutôt que «go on»). Ce verbe se situe un registre plus haut, d'où un anglais correct mais parfois raide.

pt.en: Portuguese has no phrasal verbs, so the first word that comes to mind is the Latinate one (continuar – continue rather than carry on). That verb sits a register higher, which is why correct English can still sound stiff.
pt.pt: O português não tem phrasal verbs, então a primeira palavra que vem à mente costuma ser a latina («continuar» – «continue» em vez de «carry on»). Esse verbo fica um registro acima, por isso um inglês correto ainda pode soar rígido.

errores: Pronoun after the particle: *turn on it*, *pick up it*.
Dropping the middle word of a three-part verb.
*Discuss about* — *discuss* takes no preposition, though *talk about* does.
Choosing the formal verb every time.
autochequeo: Ten different phrasal verbs — count them.
Any pronoun sitting after a particle?
Did I drop the middle word of a three-part verb?
Did any formal one-word verb slip through?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on phrasal verbs. (1) List each one and check the particle and the word order. (2) Flag every formal verb where a phrasal one would be more natural, and give it. (3) Check every pronoun position. Do not correct anything else.

es: *llevarse bien con* rendered as *take well with* instead of *get on with*.
de: *sich verstehen mit* rendered as *understand oneself with* instead of *get on with*.
it: *andare d'accordo con* rendered as *go in agreement with* instead of *get on with*.
fr: *s'entendre avec* rendered as *hear oneself with* instead of *get on with*.
pt: *dar-se bem com* rendered as *give well with* instead of *get on with*.
